plan.title: bug(acceptance): literal-AC gate re-parses ingested narrative prose as shell commands, blocking scope:complete

narratives.Description: Leftover of GitHub issue #3572 after a 0.105.0 consumer retest. Markdown blockquote greater-than is not a shell prompt; dollar-sign prompts, labeled verify lines, fences, and inline backticks stay. Never-scan of plan.narratives is out of scope.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The literal-acceptance-command gate scans xBRIEF **narrative prose** for "shell-shaped" strings and rejects them as unsafe literal AC commands. When a scope xBRIEF is created by `scope:promote --from-issue`, the ingested GitHub issue body lands verbatim in `plan.narratives.Overview` — so any quoted reviewer finding, code snippet, or blockquote in the issue becomes a permanent gate failure that blocks `scope:complete`.

The rejected text is documentation, never intended for execution.

## Concrete case

Issue #103 in our consumer repo quoted two reviewer findings verbatim. Ingest recorded them under `metadata.literal_acceptance_rejected`:

```json
{
  "command": "**P2** (50% confidence) — User/data-derived value `escapeCell(to)` interpolated into markdown bullet without newline sanitization — embedded `\\n` breaks out of the bullet and renders as a new block (CWE-116). Apply `.replace(/\\r?\\n/g, \" \")` before embedding.",
  "reason": "shell metacharacter \"(\" is not allowed in literal AC commands",
  "sourceSpan": "prompt@L11"
}
```

That string is an English sentence containing parentheses. It is not a command, was never proposed as one, and lives in a narrative field. But `scope:complete` re-parsed it on every attempt, so the story could not be closed until the blockquotes were rewritten as plain prose with an audit note recorded in `metadata`.

The same class recurred on a later story in the same session, so it is not a one-off artifact of one issue's formatting.

## Why it is worth fixing

- Any issue that quotes a reviewer finding, error message, or code fragment — i.e. most bug reports worth filing — produces a scope xBRIEF that cannot be completed without editing its own provenance record.
- The workaround degrades the artifact: the fix is to paraphrase the original issue text, which is exactly the traceability the narrative exists to preserve.
- It also produces a misleading signal. The gate reports a shell-safety violation where no command exists, so an agent reading the failure may conclude the brief proposes something dangerous.

## Suggested direction

- Scope the literal-AC scan to fields that actually carry commands (`acceptance.commands`, `metadata.literal_acceptance_commands`) and exclude `plan.narratives.*` entirely.
- If narrative scanning is deliberate, treat fenced code blocks and blockquotes as inert content rather than candidate commands.
- Persist the disposition once, rather than re-deriving the same rejection on every `scope:complete` invocation.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`, tag `v0.104.0`
- Node v22.23.2, macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- Briefs created via `deft scope:promote --from-issue=<N> --repo <owner/name>`

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T00:15:23Z)

## Triage analysis

_By: Grok 4.6 (xAI), 2026-08-20. Checked against `deftai/directive` at tag `v0.105.0` (issue body via REST, then literal-AC capture / evaluate / CHANGELOG for #3484 / #3511 / #3497)._

**Verdict:** the 0.104.0 report is accurate. As current work it is **not ready** — this class already shipped on 0.105.0. Please retest before any new story.

### Accuracy (as filed against 0.104.0)

High. Intake still scrapes narrative fields (`Overview`, `Description`, and related keys) and can stamp `plan.metadata.literal_acceptance_rejected`. The example (`sourceSpan: "prompt@L11"`, reason `shell metacharacter "("`) is exactly that scraper treating a quoted reviewer finding as a command. Re-parse on every `scope:complete` is also real (`captureFromNarratives` defaults true).

### What already shipped on 0.105.0 (2026-08-19)

This reporter’s row would be **advisory, not blocking**, on current:

- #3484 — prose-derived rejections (`prompt@` / `fence@` / `inline@` / `labeled@`) are advisory when structured commands exist
- #3511 — they stay advisory even with **no** structured `verify_commands` (this case)
- #3497 — `verify:ac` / `scope:complete` share that demotion instead of re-reading the advisory block as a brick

`isProseDerivedRejection` in `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/capture.ts` classifies `prompt@L11` as prose. `evaluate.ts` puts those on `advisoryRejected` and does not fail the gate.

### Desirability of a new story

Low until retested. Another “never scan narratives” change on top of #3484 / #3511 risks fighting the intake capture #3267 still wants for *stated* commands.

Two leftovers from this write-up are still true, and smaller:

- Narratives are still scanned on every complete. Noise, not a brick.
- #3511 already called out persist `waived` / `not_applicable` as leftover. Polish, not a new bug.

### Readiness

Not ready. Please upgrade the consumer to **0.105.0+** and retry `scope:complete` on an unedited brief that still has the quoted finding in `plan.narratives.Overview`.

- If it completes with an advisory line, this issue is fixed in 0.105.0 and should close.
- If it still blocks, that is a residual (likely a stored reject **without** `sourceSpan`). Cut a tiny leftover then; do not reopen the whole “scan narratives” story.

This is a different subsystem from #3570 / #3571 and should not share their cohort.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T00:29:08Z)

## Design critique of the triage comment (checked at `b6bc689a1fa50ea20ac050776723796de00d71a4`)

_By: Grok 4.5 (xAI)_

Checked against `origin/master` tip `b6bc689a1fa50ea20ac050776723796de00d71a4` (contains tag `v0.105.0` = `f729bf1dd29493b5d55148f97062f3a7f72a66c5`). `packages/core/src/literal-acceptance/**` matches that tip (no local drift). Allowed inputs only: issue body + triage comment `5363616951`, then file:line re-checks and a local gate repro.

### What holds

The triage's core accuracy call is right.

- Against **0.104.0**, the filed bug is real: intake still scrapes narrative prose and can stamp `plan.metadata.literal_acceptance_rejected`. Reproducing the issue's quoted-finding method on current tip, `captureLiteralAcceptanceCommandsDetailed` still rejects the English sentence with reason `shell metacharacter "(" is not allowed in literal AC commands` and a `prompt@L*` span (`capture.ts` prompt stamping ~L447).
- On **current tip**, that same persisted `sourceSpan: "prompt@L11"` row is demoted: `isProseDerivedRejection` is true (`capture.ts:854-858`), `partitionRejected` puts it on `advisoryRejected` (`evaluate.ts:65-76`), and `evaluateLiteralAcceptanceFromPlan` returns `ok: true` / `code: 0` with **zero** blocking `rejected` — even when `hasStructuredAcceptanceCommands` is false (#3511). Shared `resolveAcceptanceVerdict` then yields `empty-pass` when nothing executable ran (`acceptance-resolver.ts:125-137`).
- `scope:complete` / `verify:ac` share that path via `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` + `resolveAcceptanceGateProfile("complete")` (`acceptance-evidence.ts:515-526`, profile `captureFromNarratives: true` at `acceptance-resolver.ts:265`). #3497's advisory strip/marker exists (`LITERAL_ACCEPTANCE_ADVISORY_MARKER` at `evaluate.ts:180`).
- Desirability of a new "never scan narratives" story is correctly **low**: Overview can still carry a real stated command. Repro: Overview text containing a `$ task check` line captures `{ command: "task check", source: "task_statement", sourceSpan: "prompt@L5" }`. That is the #3267 intake-recovery job the triage refuses to reopen.

### Findings

1. **blocks-the-design** — Adopting the issue body's first suggested direction ("exclude `plan.narratives.*` entirely from the literal-AC scan") would delete stated-command recovery from Overview/Description. Measured on this tip: a narrative `$ task check` is still a live capture. The triage's refusal to open that story is the load-bearing design call; a "fix by never scanning" story would fight #3267, not finish #3572.

2. **sharpens-framing** — Span-less stored rejects still brick completion. Method: same phantom command persisted **without** `sourceSpan`, `captureFromNarratives: false` → `ok: false`, `code: 1`, blocking ledger entry with `sourceSpan: null` (`isProseDerivedRejection` returns false at `capture.ts:856`). With rescans on, the fresh `prompt@` twin becomes advisory **and** the span-less stored row remains blocking. Triage already names this residual; the sharpening is: demotion is **provenance-prefix only**, not command-text reconciliation. Close-as-fixed without the triage's retest (or a span-less leftover cut) would over-claim.

3. **sharpens-framing** — The misleading-signal complaint is only half-gone. Advisory success still appends `formatRejectedLedger`, so the message contains both `Literal acceptance advisory (#3484): … do NOT block` and nested `Literal acceptance rejected N shell-shaped command(s)` (`evaluate.ts:182-192` + `capture.ts:892-900`). Gate `ok` is true, but a headless reader skimming the nested ledger can still treat it as a brick and rewrite provenance. Polish, not a reopen of narrative scanning.

4. **footnote** — JSDoc at `evaluate.ts:25-26` says re-scan when the plan has no stored commands; `resolveRawLiteralAcceptance` actually merges narrative captures whenever `captureFromNarratives !== false` (`evaluate.ts:107-158`), including alongside a non-empty stored ledger. Comment drift only.

5. **footnote** — Complete-profile narrative re-scan remains on every `scope:complete` (`acceptance-resolver.ts:265`). Noise, as triage said — not a brick when spans are prose-prefixed.

### Existing mechanisms

Inventory before inventing anything new:

| Mechanism | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `captureLiteralAcceptanceCommandsDetailed` + intake `captureAndAttachLiteralAcceptance` | #3267 scrape + persist commands/rejects |
| `PROSE_SPAN_PREFIXES` / `isProseDerivedRejection` | #3484 provenance demotion |
| `partitionRejected` / `advisoryRejected` | blocking vs advisory split (#3484/#3511) |
| `LITERAL_ACCEPTANCE_ADVISORY_MARKER` + `stripLiteralAcceptanceAdvisory` | #3497 keep advisory text out of refusal sniffers |
| `resolveAcceptanceVerdict` / `resolveAcceptanceGateProfile` | one verify:ac / scope:complete verdict (#3497) |
| `checkIntegrated` → `captureFromNarratives: false` | avoid check-graph deadlock on prose rescans |
| CHANGELOG #3511 leftover note | `waived` / `not_applicable` ledger disposition still unshipped |

No new scanner subsystem is justified for this issue until retest falsifies the demotion on an unedited brief.

### Injection / swarm lens

- **Hostile / sloppy envelope:** omit `sourceSpan` on a persisted reject (or strip it on rewrite) and `scope:complete` fails closed again — same text that would be advisory with `prompt@`. That is the residual hazard for old or hand-edited briefs, and a footgun for any worker that "cleans" metadata.
- **Headless thrash:** advisory messages still say "rejected" in the nested ledger; a swarm leaf can burn turns paraphrasing Overview to silence noise that no longer blocks.
- **Lean that deletes narrative scan:** under headless `scope:promote --from-issue`, stated done-gates that live only in the issue Overview stop being captured. Fail-open for missing AC, or silent empty-pass pressure — worse than advisory phantoms.

### Road not taken

**Never-scan-narratives** (issue suggestion) loses measured Overview `task_statement` capture; rejected above.

**Demote every reject lacking structured provenance / demote by command-text match to a prose twin** would clear span-less residuals automatically, but also fail-open a structured unsafe command whose span was dropped. Fail-closed loses; triage's "retest, then tiny leftover if span-less" keeps the brick where provenance is unknown.

**Retest-on-0.105+ then close or cut residual** (triage) wins: preserves #3267 recovery, keeps structured rejects hard, and only spends a story if the concrete brief still bricks.

### Score against Directive rules

| Rule | Score |
| --- | --- |
| Authority ladder / claim-cites-state (#2066) | **Pass** — triage cites shipped #3484/#3511/#3497 behavior, not the issue body alone; this critique re-measured file:line + gate `ok` on the named SHA. |
| Fail-closed | **Pass** — structured / span-less unknowns still block; only prose-prefixed scrapes demote. |
| Propose-not-apply | **Pass** — triage asks for consumer retest before close or leftover cut; does not silently close. |
| Gate integrity (#3156) | **Pass** — does not propose lowering the safety allowlist to go green; uses the already-shipped demotion. |
| Thin fail-closed (#3265) | **Pass** — one demotion predicate (`isProseDerivedRejection`) + one partition; remediation is upgrade/retest, not a second parallel gate. |

### Disposition

**Uphold the triage.** Issue #3572 is **not ready** as a new "stop scanning narratives" story. Next operator action remains exactly what the triage asked: upgrade the consumer to **0.105.0+**, retry `scope:complete` on an **unedited** brief that still quotes the finding in `plan.narratives.Overview`.

- Completes with advisory only → close as fixed in 0.105.0.
- Still blocks → inspect for a stored reject **without** `sourceSpan` (or non-prose span); cut that tiny leftover — do not reopen narrative exclusion.

No model ranking. Independent open critique of comment `5363616951` only.
